## IMPORTANT — read this before running any scope check yourself

There are currently TWO independent, unrelated fix threads with uncommitted changes sitting in the SAME working tree simultaneously:

1. **This one** — a fix to `zimmColourSwatchGroup/` (the molecule), adding a `maxWidth` cap so long colour names have something to truncate against.
2. **A separate, already-independently-reviewed thread** — a fix to `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmColourSwatch/zimmColourSwatch.css.ts` (the sibling ATOM, a different file, already committed as `ab04241` and now has its own uncommitted fix on top for an unrelated focus-outline-covered-by-sibling bug). That fix already went through its own Scorer round (verdict: REWORK, for a missing test) and a follow-up implementer round just added the required test — that work is still in flight, separately, and is NOT part of what you're scoring here.

**A previous Orchestrator run scope-checking THIS truncation fix incorrectly flagged the atom file's unrelated changes as a "BLOCKED" scope violation of this round.** That was a mistake in how I (the orchestrating session) briefed it — I confirmed directly, by timeline, that the atom fix's changes predate this truncation-fix work entirely (they were already present in the file before this round's implementer was even dispatched), so there is no possible causal link. Do not repeat that mistake: when you check `git status`, you WILL see `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmColourSwatch/zimmColourSwatch.css.ts` listed as modified — that is the OTHER thread's legitimate, separately-tracked, separately-reviewed work, not scope creep from this one. Score THIS fix on whether ITS OWN two authorized files contain exactly what was asked, not on whether the shared working tree is globally clean (it won't be, by design, until both threads finish and commit separately).

## What this round changed — the two authorized files

**`zimmColourSwatchGroup.css.ts`:**
- Renamed an existing constant `PAGINATED_SWATCHES_WIDTH` → `GROUP_RESERVED_WIDTH` (same value, `calc(4 * var(--zimm-scale-1200))`, 192px) since it now backs two consumers instead of one.
- Added `maxWidth: GROUP_RESERVED_WIDTH` to the `root` part, **unconditionally** (not gated behind `isPaginated`) — confirmed by the prior Orchestrator's direct read at line 80, sitting as a plain sibling property, not inside any conditional.
- The two pre-existing `swatches` part usages (`width`/`minWidth`, gated behind `isPaginated`) were updated to the new constant name only — values and conditional logic unchanged.
- No other part (`label`, `labelName`, `pagination`, `pageButton`) was touched.

**`index.test.tsx`:** two new tests added — one asserting `root`'s `maxWidth` resolves to the expected calc() string in the non-paginated case, one confirming the same cap holds in the paginated case too (guarding against a future edit accidentally moving the cap inside the `isPaginated` conditional). Both independently read by the prior Orchestrator and confirmed non-tautological (real assertions, including an explicit `.not.toBe('none')` check). The pre-existing pagination width-stability test from an earlier round is present and unmodified.

**Why this fix exists:** a prior Tester round found, via real Chromium rendering against the live Storybook, that a long colour name (60-70+ characters) renders at full width with no truncation, because the component's `root` container has no width ceiling of its own — it auto-sizes to its widest child, so nothing constrains `labelName`'s otherwise-correct truncation CSS (`overflow:hidden; textOverflow:ellipsis; whiteSpace:nowrap`). Marcel's explicit decision: cap the component's own width to the same 192px reserved 4-swatch footprint pagination already uses, unconditionally, so truncation is self-contained regardless of what the eventual PDP page (Step 4) does or doesn't constrain.

**Real-browser proof already done, against the actual live dev Storybook (not a synthetic rebuild):** before the fix, a 70-char name rendered at ~390px with zero clipping (`scrollWidth === clientWidth`, both 351). After the fix (Storybook HMR picked up the live edit), `root` computed to exactly 192px and the name genuinely clipped (`scrollWidth 351 > clientWidth 152`). Confirmed via direct `getComputedStyle`/`getBoundingClientRect` reads in a real Chromium session, not jsdom.

```
npx tsc --noEmit          → reported 0 errors (an independent Orchestrator pass also confirmed this directly)
npm run lint               → reported unchanged baseline
npx vitest run overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmColourSwatchGroup/index.test.tsx → reported 13/13

node scripts/auditTokenUsage.mjs → reported unchanged baseline, none in this component
```

## Your job

Score against your six axes and return PASS or REWORK, evaluating ONLY this round's two authorized files and their content — not the shared working tree's overall cleanliness, which is expected to look "dirty" right now due to the separate, legitimate parallel thread explained above. If you want to independently verify the `maxWidth`/constant-rename claims yourself, do so via direct file reads and `git diff -- <specific file>` (scoped to just this round's two files), not a broad `git status` interpreted as if it only reflected this round's work. If PASS: state plainly whether this component (across ALL its accumulated fixes this build — pagination-selection resync, focus-story split, width-stability, and now this truncation cap) still owes Marcel a fresh, single consolidated visual checkpoint before final commit, or whether the real-browser proofs already gathered across these rounds are sufficient to skip a further check for this specific fix.

4	 * Recipe for the PDP colour-swatch group — the "Colour: Bay Blue" label row, and (when there is
5	 * more than one populated colour) the row of ZimmColourSwatch rectangles beneath it. This recipe
6	 * only lays the group out; each swatch's own fill/border/focus styling stays in the sibling
7	 * ZimmColourSwatch atom's own recipe.
8	 *
9	 * Values below are read directly off Figma for this exact component, not estimated — node
10	 * 40000307:13867 ("ColourOptions"), within Zimmermann_Design_System_2026.
11	 *
12	 * Six parts:
13	 *   - `root` — outer vertical flex container: the label row above, the swatches row below.
14	 *     Capped to a fixed `maxWidth` (`GROUP_RESERVED_WIDTH`, see below) unconditionally — not just
15	 *     when paginated — so `labelName`'s truncation CSS always has a definite width to truncate
16	 *     against. See this part's own baseStyle comment for the full explanation.
17	 *   - `label` — the label row ("labelContainer" in Figma): the label-group (the two
18	 *     "Colour:"/name text pieces — laid out via a plain Chakra-prop wrapper in the component
19	 *     itself, not a seventh part here; see index.tsx's own comment for why) plus the pagination
20	 *     controls, right-aligned purely via the label-group's own `flex: 1 0 0` rather than an
21	 *     absolute-position hack.
22	 *   - `labelName` — the dynamic colour-name text specifically (e.g. "Bay Blue"). Gets its own
23	 *     part, unlike the static "Colour:" piece beside it, because it alone carries the
24	 *     Figma-mandated truncation behaviour: "If Label/Colour name is longer, use truncation"
25	 *     (this node's own interaction annotation).
26	 *   - `swatches` — the horizontal row of rendered ZimmColourSwatch children. Once paginated
27	 *     (`isPaginated`), reserves a fixed page-width footprint regardless of how many items the
28	 *     current window actually renders — see its own baseStyle comment below for the layout bug
29	 *     this prevents.
30	 *   - `pagination` — wrapper around the two chevron buttons.
31	 *   - `pageButton` — each individual chevron button (24x24, holding a 16px ZimmIcon).
32	 */
33	
34	/**
35	 * Matches `SWATCHES_PER_PAGE` in this component's own index.tsx (Figma's own interaction
36	 * annotation: "Pagination appears if there are more than 4 swatches"). Kept as its own literal
37	 * here rather than imported across files — this recipe stays a self-contained, co-located file,
38	 * the same precedent the sibling zimmColourSwatch.css.ts already sets for a state-dependent
39	 * baseStyle function. If `SWATCHES_PER_PAGE` in index.tsx ever changes, update this to match.
40	 */
41	const PAGE_SIZE = 4;
42	
43	/**
44	 * The reserved 4-swatch-wide footprint: PAGE_SIZE swatches at the atom's own fixed 48px width
45	 * (`--zimm-scale-1200` — see zimmColourSwatch.css.ts's `swatch.width`), with no per-swatch gap
46	 * (`swatches.gap` below is 0, same as the atom's own adjacency). Two consumers share this one
47	 * value rather than each typing their own copy of the same `calc(...)` expression:
48	 *   - `swatches.width`/`minWidth`, applied only once paginated (see that part below) — keeps the
49	 *     footprint constant across a full page vs. a shorter final page.
50	 *   - `root.maxWidth`, applied unconditionally regardless of pagination (see that part below) —
51	 *     caps the whole component so `labelName`'s truncation CSS always has a definite width to
52	 *     truncate against.
53	 */
54	const GROUP_RESERVED_WIDTH = `calc(${PAGE_SIZE} * var(--zimm-scale-1200))`;
55	
56	export const ZimmColourSwatchGroup = {
57	  parts: ['root', 'label', 'labelName', 'swatches', 'pagination', 'pageButton'],
58	
59	  baseStyle: ({ isPaginated }: { isPaginated?: boolean }): Record<string, SystemStyleObject> => ({
60	    root: {
61	      display: 'flex',
62	      flexDirection: 'column',
63	      // 8px between the label row and the swatches row. No background here — background lives
64	      // per-swatch, already handled by the atom's own recipe.
65	      gap: 'var(--zimm-scale-xs)',
66	      // Unconditional cap, regardless of `isPaginated` — this is a bug fix, not a stylistic
67	      // choice. `root` otherwise has no width of its own (deliberate — see the `swatches` part
68	      // below for why a short, non-paginated row must still size naturally to its actual content)
69	      // so it has no ceiling for `labelName`'s truncation CSS to truncate against: confirmed via
70	      // real Chromium rendering that a long enough colour name simply grows `root` (and the
71	      // flex-grown `labelName` span inside it) past this footprint with no ellipsis, unless some
72	      // ancestor happens to impose a definite width of its own. Capping `root` itself to the same
73	      // reserved footprint `swatches` already reserves once paginated makes truncation
74	      // self-contained in every context, rather than depending on whatever the eventual PDP page
75	      // does or doesn't constrain. `maxWidth`, not `width`: `root` must still be free to render
76	      // narrower than this when content is short (e.g. one or two short colour names) — this only
77	      // ever stops it from growing past the cap. Does not change the swatches row's own sizing
78	      // behaviour (still `100%` when non-paginated, see below) — it only changes what that `100%`
79	      // now resolves against.
80	      maxWidth: GROUP_RESERVED_WIDTH,
81	    },
82	
83	    label: {
84	      display: 'flex',
85	      alignItems: 'center',
86	      // 24px. Matches spacing.xl exactly, so the named step is used rather than the numerically
87	      // identical --zimm-scale-600 alias — see bottomBar.css.ts's own `var(--zimm-scale-xl)`
88	      // usage for the same 24px value elsewhere in this codebase.
89	      height: 'var(--zimm-scale-xl)',
90	      // 8px between the label-group and the pagination controls.
91	      gap: 'var(--zimm-scale-xs)',
92	    },
93	
94	    labelName: {
95	      textStyle: 'caption',
96	      color: 'var(--zimm-color-text-default)',
97	      // The truncating half of the label-group's two text pieces (the static "Colour:" text
98	      // beside it never truncates — see index.tsx). `flex: 1 0 0` lets it consume the
99	      // label-group's remaining width; `minWidth: 0` is required for a flex item to actually
100	      // shrink below its content size instead of overflowing; the rest is the standard
101	      // single-line-ellipsis triad.
102	      flex: '1 0 0',
103	      minWidth: 0,
104	      overflow: 'hidden',
105	      textOverflow: 'ellipsis',
106	      whiteSpace: 'nowrap',
107	    },
108	
109	    swatches: {
110	      display: 'flex',
111	      // Non-paginated (<= SWATCHES_PER_PAGE populated colours): sizes naturally to however many
112	      // swatches are actually present. Unchanged, deliberately out of scope for this fix — there
113	      // is no confirmed design value either way for a 2- or 3-colour row's width, so nothing was
114	      // invented here.
115	      //
116	      // Paginated (> SWATCHES_PER_PAGE populated colours, windowed to a fixed PAGE_SIZE-wide
117	      // slice per page): a plain `100%` here resolves against `root`'s own width — but `root` has
118	      // no explicit width of its own, so it auto-fits to its widest child, which is this very
119	      // element. That circular relationship meant the *rendered* width tracked how many items the
120	      // current window actually held (192px for a full 4-item page, 96px for a 2-item final
121	      // page), so `root` — and `label` above it, itself 100% of that same `root` — visibly
122	      // resized between pages. Confirmed directly in a running Storybook: the pagination chevrons
123	      // jumped position between the two pages of the `Paginated` story. Reserving
124	      // GROUP_RESERVED_WIDTH regardless of the current page's real item count breaks that
125	      // loop — the footprint stays constant across every page, full or partial. A partial final
126	      // page's unused space simply remains empty to the right: the flex default
127	      // `justify-content: flex-start` already left-aligns the rendered items, so nothing further
128	      // is needed for that.
129	      width: isPaginated ? GROUP_RESERVED_WIDTH : '100%',
130	      ...(isPaginated ? { minWidth: GROUP_RESERVED_WIDTH } : {}),
131	      // Confirmed directly off the Figma export, not a stylistic default: the 4-swatch example
132	      // measures exactly 192px total width for four 48px-wide swatches (4 x 48, no gap
133	      // contribution) — swatches sit directly adjacent. Do not add a gap here; that would be a
134	      // real deviation from the design, not a stylistic default.
135	      gap: 0,
136	    },
137	
138	    pagination: {
139	      display: 'flex',
140	      alignItems: 'center',
141	      // No inter-button gap value exists in the Figma export handed to this step — left at the
142	      // flex default (no `gap` declared at all) rather than invented. Revisit if a designer
143	      // confirms a real value.
144	    },
145	
146	    pageButton: {
147	      display: 'flex',
148	      alignItems: 'center',
149	      justifyContent: 'center',
150	      width: 'var(--zimm-scale-xl)', // 24px
151	      height: 'var(--zimm-scale-xl)', // 24px
152	      // Resets the native <button> UA chrome so the box is exactly the 24x24 the design calls

155	      border: 'none',

157	      cursor: 'pointer',

164	      _disabled: {

166	      },

I independently confirmed the framing is accurate: `git status` shows only `zimmColourSwatch/index.test.tsx`, `zimmColourSwatch/zimmColourSwatch.css.ts` (the atom, other thread) and `theme/components/index.ts` (the pre-existing `ZimmColourSwatchGroup` recipe registration — its diff adds only that one import/key, consistent with an earlier round of *this* component, not the atom thread) as modified, plus the whole `zimmColourSwatchGroup/` directory as untracked. I scored only the two files named for this round, read in full, not the tree as a whole.

## Per-axis table

| Axis | Verdict | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| **Design fidelity** | UNVERIFIED (by me) | No browser tool available to me in this session, and no committed artifact (screenshot, Playwright trace, story with a long name) exists for me to inspect. I independently confirmed the *math* is real, not invented — `--zimm-scale-1200` = `48px` in `overrides/app/theme/foundation/zimmTokens.ts:166`, matching the atom's own `swatch.width` — so `GROUP_RESERVED_WIDTH` genuinely is "4 real swatch-widths," not a guessed number. I also reasoned through the flexbox mechanics (unconditional `max-width` only clamps an upper bound, never forces a box wider) and it's consistent with the claimed before/after behaviour. But I did not render this myself, so the Tester's Chromium proof is PLAUSIBLE, not CONFIRMED by me. |
| **Completeness** | PASS, with a gap flagged | Test is present, comprehensive, and passing (13/13, confirmed by my own run). No story/named export exists anywhere in `index.stories.tsx` demonstrating the long-name truncation state this whole fix targets — every existing story (`Default`, `Paginated`, etc.) uses short names (Bay Blue, Ivory, Black...). Not a hard rule violation (a per-state story is judgment, not mandatory), but it's the one artifact that would let a human confirm this Figma-mandated behaviour without live-editing Storybook Controls. |
| **Correctness** | PASS | `tsc --noEmit`: 0 errors (reproduced myself). Targeted test: 13/13 (reproduced myself). Full suite: reproduced myself at **28 files / 432 tests, all green** — close to but not identical to the reported "29/433"; immaterial to the verdict (both are 100% green) but the report's count doesn't match what I measured. `npm run lint`: reproduced myself — 4 pre-existing errors (`routes.tsx`, `recipeGuards.test.ts`) and assorted warnings, **none in this component or either in-flight thread** (confirmed by cross-referencing against `git status`, since neither file is modified on this branch). `audit:tokens`: reproduced myself — 4 unacknowledged violations, all in `header.ts`/`header/index.tsx`/`navConstants.ts`, none in this component. |
| **Conformance** | PASS | Every value in the diff is `var(--zimm-*)` or a `calc()` wrapping one — no bare token keys, no raw hex/px/rem literals. `recipeGuards.test.ts` (read in full, then reproduced passing 6/6) walks the registered recipe map including `ZimmColourSwatchGroup`; `maxWidth` is in its `SIZING_PROPS` set, and `GROUP_RESERVED_WIDTH`'s calc string doesn't match any bare `SPACING_KEYS` entry, so it's mechanically clean, not just visually clean. Namespacing (`ZimmColourSwatchGroup`, no base-SFCC collision) and co-location pattern both correct. |
| **Restraint** | PASS | Read both files in full (176 + 283 lines). The `css.ts` diff is exactly: rename `PAGINATED_SWATCHES_WIDTH`→`GROUP_RESERVED_WIDTH`, add `maxWidth: GROUP_RESERVED_WIDTH` to `root` (confirmed unconditional — sits as a plain sibling property, no ternary), and mechanically update the two existing `swatches` references to the new name. No other part touched. Test diff is exactly the two described new tests appended after the existing, unmodified pagination-width test. |
| **Pass criteria** | PASS | The step's own ask — rename the constant, cap `root` unconditionally, prove it both ways — is met and directly verified against the file contents, not asserted. |

## Overall: PASS

## What I tried to falsify

- **Tried to break the "unconditional maxWidth is free" claim.** Walked the actual CSS mechanics for the non-clamped case (root shrink-to-fits below 192px, `max-width` never binds, unaffected) and for a hypothetical clamped-but-few-swatches case (a name long enough to want >192px, but only 2–3 swatches, whose own natural width is 96–144px). In that case `swatches: width: '100%'` would resolve against the now-192px-clamped `root`, potentially leaving visible trailing empty space after the last swatch. I then checked whether this is a *new* regression from this fix — it isn't: before this fix, `root` was already sized to `max(label's content width, swatches' content width)`, so a long label already stretched `swatches` past its natural width via the same `100%` relationship, just to a larger, uncapped number. This fix bounds that pre-existing behaviour rather than introducing it. I could not fully rule out that the bounded 192px trailing-space case looks wrong against Figma for that specific combination — nobody's evidence, including the Tester's, mentions checking a low-swatch-count case, only the default 3-swatch set with a 70-char name.
- **Tried to falsify the "these are the only two files that changed" claim.** Read every line of both files rather than trusting the diff summary, and cross-checked `git status` against the claimed separate-thread narrative — the modified/untracked file list matches the claim exactly (atom thread's two files, this component's own earlier-round theme registration, and this round's untracked molecule directory), so I found no scope leakage.
- **Tried to falsify the "not a magic number" claim.** Grepped the actual token value backing the whole calc() rather than trusting the recipe's comment — confirmed `--zimm-scale-1200` is genuinely `48px`, matching the atom's own swatch width, so `4 × 48 = 192` is a real derivation, not an invented figure.
- **Tried to falsify "unchanged lint/audit baseline."** Ran both myself rather than trusting the report. Lint does fail overall, but on two files (`routes.tsx`, `recipeGuards.test.ts`) neither thread touches — genuinely pre-existing, confirmed via `git status`. Nothing in the actual lint or audit output mentions `zimmColourSwatchGroup`.
- **Tried to falsify the test suite's non-tautology claim.** Confirmed the two new tests assert a real, Figma-derived literal value and explicitly assert `.not.toBe('none')` — a test that would catch a reversion of this exact fix, not one that would pass regardless of implementation.

## What I could not verify

- **No browser tool available to me.** I could not reproduce the Tester's Chromium session myself (computed `maxWidth`, real clipping via `scrollWidth`/`clientWidth`). I'm relying on their described result plus my own CSS-mechanics reasoning, which is consistent with it — that's PLAUSIBLE, not CONFIRMED.
- **The few-swatches + long-but-not-extreme-name interaction** (trailing empty space in the `swatches` row when `root` clamps but swatch count is 2–3) — not covered by any test, not mentioned as checked by the Tester, and I have no Figma access in this session to confirm whether that combination has a spec at all.
- **The exact "29 files / 433 tests" figure** — I measured 28/432 (both fully green); didn't chase the one-test/one-file discrepancy further since it doesn't change the pass/fail outcome, but flagging it since accurate reporting matters even when the bottom line agrees.

## Defects

None CONFIRMED or PLAUSIBLE-and-blocking in the two authorized files. Two non-blocking follow-ups, not required for this round's PASS:

- `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmColourSwatchGroup/index.stories.tsx` — no named story exercises a long `selectedName`. Suggest adding one (e.g. `LongColourName: Story`) using the same 70-char string the test uses, so the Figma-mandated truncation behaviour has a durable, reviewable visual artifact instead of living only in a jsdom computed-style assertion.
- Same file — consider adding a `FewSwatchesLongName` variant (2 swatches + a long name) specifically to visually settle the trailing-space question raised above before it's forgotten.

## Biggest residual risk in shipping this step

**None of the real-browser verification across this component's four accumulated fixes (pagination-selection resync, focus-story split, width-stability, and now this truncation cap) has ever been done in one combined pass against the current, final state of the file** — each was checked in isolation, by the Tester, at the time that specific bug was found. The specific interaction I flagged above (a long name clamping `root` while `swatches`'s pre-existing `width: '100%'` is also live) sits exactly at the seam between the width-stability fix and this truncation fix, and nothing in the evidence gathered so far demonstrates those two were ever exercised together in a real layout engine.

**Direct answer to the closing question: yes, this still owes Marcel one fresh, consolidated visual checkpoint before final commit** — not because any individual fix looks wrong, but because it's never been looked at whole. Recommend one real-browser pass (Storybook's `Default` story, live-editing the `selectedName` control) covering: (1) a 70-char name with the default 3–4 swatches (confirms this round), (2) a moderately long name with only 2 swatches (settles the trailing-space question), and (3) paging back and forth with a long name selected (confirms the pagination-resync and truncation fixes don't fight each other). That's cheap to do now and is exactly the kind of check that no amount of additional jsdom-based test-writing can substitute for.
